Maya,

Appreciate the context and the competitor PDF — thanks for sharing. High-level, we can match the effective rate for the pilot with a conditional, staggered migration credit and a 10-day ops sprint during cutover.

Proposed playbook (initial):
- One-time migration credit: equivalent to ~3 months of expected spend, paid as a credit over 3 invoices (phased).
- Ops sprint: 2-week dedicated handoff with our SREs + a playbook for KV-cache priming and throughput tuning.
- SLA uplift: First 90 days with priority capacity and rollback options if latency targets are missed.

If that fits, I can draft a simple playbook and pricing memo for procurement. Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow (Tue) at 10am PT?

I attached a quick draft workbook — Draft_Playbook.xlsx — with the math baseline; jonas and laura are looped for approvals and the legal/terms check.

Forwarding Maya's request — quick internal assessment below.

On Mon, 28 Jun 2027 at 09:10, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmeretail.com> wrote:
> (see attached competitor quote)

Internal notes / recommended structure:
- Baseline economics: if Acme runs 80M tokens/mo, their run-rate is ~ $X/month (see Draft_Playbook worksheet). A 3-month equivalent credit at that run-rate buys runway and reduces churn risk.
- Proposed credit envelope: $90k–$140k one-time, phased over first 3 invoices; final figure depends on true monthly token baseline and whether we take on any overage protection.
- SLA carveouts: prioritize capacity for 90 days (no queueing above baseline) + one rollback window (30 days) for major regressions. Avoid placing open-ended outage credits; prefer scoped SLA KPIs with remediation steps.
- Legal: need a short sideletter and a DocuSign flow; laura to confirm wording for suspension/rollback triggers.

Questions for Neha: do we want to offer an accelerated onboarding discount (one-time) or a blended rate for 6 months? Which has a better retention signal from Acme?

-Jonas
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

Thanks — ran the numbers and spoke to legal. My refined recommendation:

- Migration credit: $120,000 one-time, applied as 3 equal credits across invoices 1–3 (conditional on hitting onboarding milestones A/B/C in the playbook).
- Ops sprint: 10 business days (onsite/remote hybrid) during cutover with a named SRE and runbook; success criteria documented in the playbook.
- Blended rate: We will match competitor effective rate for the first 90 days; after that default to contracted tiered consumption.
- SLA: Priority capacity for 90 days; performance remediation is limited to credit remediation (no automatic terminations). Legal prefers a short sideletter and the DocuSign route — they can sign acceptance for the playbook rather than a full contract amendment.

I attached a one-page terms summary for procurement to review (terms_summary.pdf). Once Neha confirms willingness to offer $120k I can trigger legal and the DocuSign envelope.

-Laura
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
